hed: Oil slips Friday but week holds above $100; U.S. diesel hits record as Mocha + Hormuz squeeze persists
dek: Brent crude traded near $104–$106 a barrel and WTI near $99–$101 on Friday after slipping from Thursday’s highs, with Reuters and CNBC reporting both benchmarks still on track to finish the week above $100 for the first time since mid-May. Markets continued to price the dual chokepoint squeeze: Iran-aligned Houthis’ advances near Bab el-Mandeb and the U.S.–Iran tanker war constraining Hormuz flows. U.S. diesel prices hit a record national average above $6 a gallon, adding to inflation and shipping-cost fears even as crude pared some midweek gains.

cl.body: Reuters, CNBC, and Bloomberg frame Friday’s pullback — Brent near $104–$106, WTI near $99–$101 in early/midday prints — against record U.S. diesel above $6 a gallon and warnings that refined products may keep rising even if crude chops, as Hormuz transit stays depressed and Middle East supply gaps feed inflation talk.

cr.body: The National and Reuters energy desks stress that despite Friday’s slip from Thursday’s surge, Brent and WTI remain on pace for a weekly finish above $100 as Houthi control near Mocha/Bab el-Mandeb and Hormuz tanker attacks keep dual-chokepoint risk elevated for Gulf and Red Sea export routes.

stack_blurb: Brent ~$104–106 / WTI ~$99–101 Fri; week >$100; U.S. diesel record.
seo_description: Oil slipped Friday but Brent near $104–106 and WTI near $99–101 still pointed to a weekly finish above $100 as Mocha/Hormuz risks persisted and U.S. diesel hit a record.
